pr.title: Plan running the full gate once per head, in CI
pr.head: 16f042be5af977fce9bba15ff65d62b1f33526d5

summary: Projector's skills tell three parties to run a repository's full validation gate, its complete set of tests and checks, on every head of a pull request. The author or the fixer runs it before each push, CI runs it on the push, and the reviewer runs it again, through project review gate when review.gate is set in .projector.toml, or from the repository's instructions otherwise. Two of those three runs check code that was already checked.

This pull request adds only a plan, docs/projects/gate-in-ci/readme.md, at status: ready. The plan adds a review.gate_checks setting that names the GitHub Actions check runs that run a repository's suite. Where the setting is set:

• The author and the fixer run the tests that cover their change and the review.gate command before a push, not the full suite.
  • The reviewer runs project review gate, which waits up to 30 minutes for the named check runs on the head and writes their result into the same gate record a local run writes. So the incremental review's rule, which asks for a passing gate when the merge base moved, reads a CI result without change.
  • The watch daemon sends a new CHECKS event to the fixer when the head's CI rollup fails.

A head that changes a file under .github/workflows/ wrote the workflow CI ran, so gate refuses to use CI for it and the reviewer runs the full gate locally. A repository without the setting keeps today's behavior. The code, skills, and docs follow in a later pull request.

cards.title: What the gate's exit codes mean
cards.html:
ExitWhenWhat the reviewer does
0The review.gate command passed and every named check concluded successCounts the gate as passed
1The command failed, or a named check concluded anything elseTreats it as a failing gate
75A named check had no completed run within 30 minutesReviews by reading and discloses that CI had not finished

groups.title: The plan for running the gate in CI
groups.kicker: The problem, the new setting, the gate's CI wait, and the CHECKS event
intro: The plan is the whole change. § 2.1 walks through the flow after the change, step by step. § 2.2 defines the review.gate_checks setting, the two fields the gate record gains (checks and source), and the CHECKS event line. § 2.3 lists the change to each file.

A check run is GitHub's record of one CI job on a commit. A commit status is a simpler state that any account with write access can post, which is how Projector posts its own projector/review sign-off. The rollup is GitHub's single state across both kinds. The plan counts only check runs from the github-actions app for the gate, so a commit status, Projector's own included, never counts as test evidence. The watch event reads the rollup instead.

checks.text: A plan at ready claims it is executable, so every question that blocks implementation must be answered or deferred. Its two open questions, a configurable wait and merge-queue checks, are deferred in § 6, and § 5 defers measuring the watch query's cost to the implementation.

files.note: The new plan: why the gate runs three times today, how the CI gate works, and how each skill changes.

checks.text: The refusal covers only .github/workflows/. A workflow step uses: ./.github/actions/test runs the local composite action as the pull request spells it, so a head that edits that action defines what CI ran and still gets a passing CI gate. The review asks the check to cover all of .github/, or .github/actions/ as well.

Exit 75 comes after the same 30-minute wait whether a check is still running or has no run at all, as after a renamed job or a typo in the setting. Then the review proceeds by reading, so each full review of a trusted head can sign off without running any test, though § 3 rejects signing off with no evidence. The review asks for a local full gate on exit 75 instead.

The rollup includes commit statuses, and Projector posts projector/review as failure on each changes-requested head where a ruleset requires it, as this repository's does. So every such review would send the fixer a CHECKS failure with no run log to read. The review asks to decide CHECKS from the contexts and leave out projector/review.

The check-runs endpoint returns 30 runs a page by default, and the plan reads one page. On a commit with more runs, such as a matrix build, the named check can be missed, and the gate waits 30 minutes and exits 75 though the check passed. The review asks for the endpoint's check_name filter or pagination.
